reason: Depth of a leaf tooth (how deep it cuts) is a real measurable trait; the examples are correct.
Spore outline in equatorial or polar view can be semicircular; the examples fit.
Oblong teeth are a normal leaf-tooth shape; the examples fit.
The examples say 'rounded' (a round or globose tuber), not obtuse. Obtuse describes an apex angle, so this is a wrong reading. A round-shape term would be correct.
The abaxial surface of the petiole can be glabrous. The examples are about the surface, though the bearer is really the petiole surface.
'Dorsal' here gives the position of sori on the veinlets or the frond back. That is a position, not a quality of the sorus. A rule would need to map it to a position or relation pattern.
'7-10 mm wide' is a measured width, not an increased width. It should go to plain width. The pair is a wrong reading.
Lobes and coronal scales can be elliptic; the examples are correct.
'Rays few' means few ray flowers per head. The bearer should be the head, not the ray flower, because a ray flower cannot have fewer parts of its own type. Wrong part.
'Large' is relative to the organ and the taxon, and the examples cover different parts (opening, lobe). A rule would need the specific part and a size reference.
Length is a valid quality; 'a × b mm' gives length and width. The bearer is a generic FLOPO class, so check it is the right part.
'Foot 3-4 mm long' is a measured length, not an increased length. It should go to plain length. Wrong reading.
The distance between sori ('2 mm apart') is a valid and common trait.
A pale costa is a colour description (low saturation or lightness); the examples fit.
The examples say the branch bears tendrils. That is has-part tendril, not a quality of the branch. A rule for 'with X' should give the part.
The presence of cyathia is a normal presence statement; the examples fit.
Spatulate is a normal shape for leaves, lobes and petals, in English and French.
Cuspidate apices are normal in plants; the examples fit.
'Subglobose' pollinia map reasonably to spheroid.
Leaf scars can be inconspicuous; the examples fit.
Racemes can be cylindrical.
Pilosity is the PATO attribute; the examples (villous, puberulent, hirsute) are its values. The attribute is acceptable, though a rule could map these to specific values.
'Hooked hairs' and 'uncinulé' describe the hairs, not a sickle-shaped peduncle. Falciform is the wrong meaning here.
Ridged surfaces on fruits, stones and stems are a normal trait.
Blotched fruit or endocarp is a valid colour pattern.
Paraphyses and their cells can be transparent.
Only one flora, and fasciation is a rare malformation. 'Fasciated' may be a translation of fasciculate (stamens in bundles). A rule would need to tell malformation from bundled stamens.
Hairy on surfaces or margins is a normal trait.
A persistent style is a normal fruit trait.
'Glabrate with age' is a hair-cover statement, which pilosity covers. Keep the 'with age' context in mind.
The examples count sporocarps per frond. A count of sporocarps does not belong to an indumentum-type class. Wrong part.
Flower buds can be cylindrical.
Furrowed achenes are a common trait.
Caudate apices are a standard shape.
Twisted or contorted stamens (tordus) are a valid trait.
Winged corollas or corolla tubes occur (e.g. in the Gentianaceae); the examples fit.
'Stellate' describes the trichomes on the hypanthium, not the shape of the hypanthium. Wrong reading. The trichomes should be the bearer.
The examples mix a flared sheath scar with 'empâté/empattement' (a swollen base). The word does not mean 'flared' for a stem. A rule would need to separate the two senses.
'Rounded in cross section' is a round section, not an obtuse shape. Wrong reading.
A bumpy lemma surface is a texture; knobbled is close enough.
Orbicular sporangia are a valid shape.
The examples mix absence ('absent'), ornaments and callus descriptions. A rule would need to tell presence of the part from descriptions of its parts.
An undivided sepal (margin) is a normal trait.
Presence of vegetative or leaf buds in axils is a valid statement.
A semicircular contraligule is a valid shape in grasses.
A semicircular scutellum is a valid shape.
'Rather thin' describes sporangium wall thickness. It is a single example, so check it.
A compact strobilus is a valid density trait.
Megaspore surface texture (papillate, tuberculate) is standard in ferns and lycophytes.
'Uniseriate' and 'plurisériées' usually describe rows of pappus bristles or phyllaries, not the ray flower itself. Wrong part.
Sessile umbels are a valid trait.
The statement is about the base of the umbel (or its axis). Only one flora. A rule would need to tell the whole umbel from its base or stalk.
Sizes of 2-6 mm are too small for a whole umbel. They probably belong to the fruit, flower or umbellule. A rule would need to find the real bearer.
Large areoles are a standard cactus trait.
The orientation of a leaf margin (recurved, plane) is valid. Some examples are about teeth, so check them.
Columella width is a normal measurement.
'Geniculate' or 'angled' for a whole plant usually means the stems or culms, not the plant. A rule would need to move it to the stem.
Fruit pedicel diameter is a normal measurement.
Follicle diameter is a normal measurement.
Inconspicuous rhizoids are a valid description in bryophytes.
